items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I hated so much when I was associated with Selmer and that Varitone.

ctx.x: That – the Varitone? I got hooked up in that, and I’m so sorry that I got messed up in that, because it caused a kid to rely on electricity before he reached a point where he had found the center of his tone. It takes a while to develop an embouchure and get the point where you know [Terry buzzes his lips] right where the center of your tone comes from, from the standpoint of the formation of your embouchure. If a kid doesn’t do that – you can just put that thing up there and say [Terry blows air, without buzzing…

Your son Tony was saying earlier that he thinks the reason why you have such a strong embouchure goes back to the fact that early on, when you were making instruments out of tubing, that – because the back end of the tube is flat, that it forced you to have a very tight formed embouchure, simply using the musculature of your face.
